items.title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science? | Science
items.snippet: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, ala...
items.raw_snippet: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI [...] AI with an aligned purpose for sustainability of all life within the relational frameworks of Indigenous knowledge could build a technology that serves the planet. Such a shift would reposition a future form of AI as a critical mechanism for the stewardship of all life on Earth. [...] and use of knowledge. In its current form and design, AI is effectively the outcome of multiple permutations of statistical calculations conveying statistically weighted output and trained to generate practical outcomes. However, within Indigenous scientific systems, there is no “right answer” without an initial, ethically aligned purpose and process. Therefore, “what is the point” is the point.
